[ASSISTANT_SAID] Common misconceptions about yoga include:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Yoga is only for flexible people: Yoga is designed to help build flexibility, strength, and balance over time.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Yoga is just stretching: Yoga involves mindful movements, meditation, breathwork, and relaxation techniques.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Yoga is religious: Yoga can be enjoyed by anyone, regardless of their faith or beliefs.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Yoga is only for women: Yoga is excellent for everyone, regardless of gender.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. Yoga is too slow and boring: There are many styles of yoga that are challenging, dynamic, and energizing.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 6. Yoga is expensive: There are many affordable or free options available online or in the community.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 7. You need a lot of equipment to practice yoga: You can practice yoga anywhere with just your body and comfortable clothing.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Tips for beginners interested in trying yoga include:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Start with a beginner-friendly class designed for new practitioners.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Listen to your body and avoid pushing too hard to prevent injury.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Don't worry about being "good" at yoga; focus on your own practice.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Use props like blocks and straps for support when starting out.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. Find a teacher you connect with for a better experience.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Yoga is a journey that takes time; be patient and have fun.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Advice for keeping up with a yoga class includes:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Don't be afraid to take breaks when needed.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Focus on your breath to stay calm and centered.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Modify poses using props or adjust your posture for comfort.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Practice at home to build confidence and familiarize with poses.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. Remember that everyone's journey is different
